subject: Alignment request: standard uptime, latency SLOs and tiered monthly credit ceiling — StratumPay
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Draft approach for StratumPay SLA ceiling / uptime bands

Team —

Quick summary: StratumPay (procurement) sent back an SLA redline that pushes for a 99.95% baseline and wants the monthly service credit cap to be 25% of monthly fees. They cited enterprise parity and their internal risk matrix. Legal asked us to propose a compromise that preserves our operational guardrails while keeping the commercial ask reasonable.

My suggested starting point (so we can be decisive before the Friday call with Alex):
- Baseline uptime: 99.9% (standard hosted tier)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-model text generation (region: us-west)
- Monthly service credit trigger: any monthly uptime below 99.9%
- Credit ladder: 99.5–99.9% = 5% credit; 99.0–99.49% = 15% credit; <99.0% = 30% credit (capped at 30% of monthly recurring charges)
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (with >72h notice window) and force majeure per the template

Why this: keeps us in line with product economics and caps exposure. The 30% top cap is firm for us — anything higher starts to materially affect unit economics for reserved clusters.

Open asks:
1) Ben — are the numbers above operationally safe for Dedicated pools if we allow StratumPay to have burst capacity?
2) Laura/legal — is 30% an acceptable ceiling to push in negotiation, or do we need a tiered escrow/escrow-lite mechanism instead?
3) Aditya/eng — can we commit to the latency SLO above for their expected workload (they said ~3M tokens/month at launch)?

I'll draft a short counterproposal doc and send it to Alex with marked trade-offs. If we agree, I'll include the RNWd counter spreadsheet as an attachment.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment request: standard uptime, latency SLOs and tiered monthly credit ceiling — StratumPay

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick summary and suggested banding. A few clarifying points from our side after legal reviewed:
- StratumPay target is to avoid any single-vendor availability exposure beyond 15% monthly credit at the very worst. Their board expects a hard cap of 15%.
- They are willing to accept 99.9% baseline but would like the top credit cap to be 15% with a graded ladder (we proposed 5%/10%/15%).
- They asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary higher availability commitment for the first 90 days (we are in ramp) — e.g., enhanced SLA of 99.95% for the onboarding window — in exchange for a 12-month term and a 10% annual commitment increase.

Attached we’ve included a marked redline (StratumPay_SLA_redline_20260512.pdf) with their edits and a short note from procurement on acceptable alternatives. If you can respond with a counter that includes a clear operational tradeoff section, that will speed approvals on our end.

Appreciate it —
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships | StratumPay
alex.turner@stratumpay.com
Attachment: StratumPay_SLA_redline_20260512.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stratumpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment request: standard uptime, latency SLOs and tiered monthly credit ceiling — StratumPay

Alex —

Appreciate the context and the redline. Quick reply while we align internally:
- We can accept a 15% maximum cap in principle, provided we narrow the trigger windows and maintain stronger carveouts. Specifically: no credit for partial degraded latency if core control-plane remains healthy; credits measured monthly and tied to aggregated customer-impacting outages (not transient single-AZ incidents under our ops playbook).
- The temporary 99.95% onboarding uplift is something we can discuss but it requires a clear burst capacity reservation and a 10% committed spend uplift (you mentioned 10% — we need a contractual minimum to rely on). That uplift also needs to be constrained to a 90-day window with a defined rollback if utilization is lower than expected.
- Proposed counter (attached): RNWd_SLA_counterproposal_20260513.xlsx — it shows two options: (A) 99.9% baseline with 15% cap and tightened carveouts; (B) 99.95% 90-day onboarding uplift in exchange for a 10% commit uplift and limited reserved burst pool.

I've asked Ben to confirm the operational feasibility for option B and Laura to flag any legal issues with the escrow/measurement language.

On process: if StratumPay is OK with (A) we can route to legal for a quick signature cycle. If they prefer (B) we'll need a short technical addendum and a 5–7 business day lead time for capacity reservation approvals.

Thanks —
Hannah

Subject: Re: Alignment request: standard uptime, latency SLOs and tiered monthly credit ceiling — StratumPay

Alex / Hannah / team —

Ben from infra here. Confirming operational notes on option B (99.95% onboarding uplift):
- We can provision a dedicated burst pool for 90 days, but it requires a signed addendum and a 10% committed spend uplift to justify reserved capacity. Lead time: 7 business days after signature to schedule GPU reservations and network routes.
- Measurement: we will instrument a separate monitoring tag for StratumPay traffic and report p95/p99 latency weekly during the uplift window. Any credits for availability will be based on cross-AZ outage impact aggregated over the month. Transient single-AZ latency spikes are excluded as long as failover worked per runbook.
- Ops risk: the uplift increases cost exposure for Redwood for the 90-day window — the 10% minimum commit mitigates this. For long-term, option A (99.9% baseline with 15% cap) is materially safer.

Next steps: Hannah to confirm which option StratumPay prefers. If (A), legal can fast-track the standard amendment. If (B), we'll prepare the technical addendum and an ops checklist (I'll share by Monday).

Ben Carter
VP, Infrastructure Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
